# FDG7066

> DO provide an exception-throwing member for each member using the Try Pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.5.2 The Try Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Analyzer candidate rejected: the throwing member can have another name or be an indexer (TryGetValue and the indexer of a dictionary), and the Mariani annotation advises against members that nobody could reasonably use.

## From the book

```csharp
public struct DateTime {
  public static DateTime Parse(string dateTime){ ... }
  public static bool TryParse(string dateTime, out DateTime result){
... }
}
```

> **Rico Mariani:** But don’t provide members that nobody could reasonably use. There’s no reason to set your clients up for failure by giving them an API that’s almost guaranteed to be too slow to use. The most obvious way to use your system should also be the best way.
